name: Omex Corporate Services Staff Polo
description:
The standard-issue polo shirt for Omex Corporate Services client-facing staff — the people who work the desks, check credentials, manage building access, and smile at you while deciding whether to let you through. The fabric is a smooth, moisture-wicking synth-blend that photographs well under office lighting and stays unwrinkled through a twelve-hour shift. The Omex wordmark is embroidered in silver thread on the left chest, and a discreet employee ID slot is sewn into the right cuff. The collar is stiff enough to look formal, soft enough not to chafe.

The polo comes in three colorways depending on department: slate blue for reception and client services, charcoal for facilities management, and white for executive floor support. Wearing the wrong color in the wrong department is a formal HR incident. Staff receive two per year; extras can be purchased at cost through the company store.
functionality: Integrated RFID cuff slot for employee ID chip; fabric treated for stain resistance and press retention.
what_it_says: You work for Omex. That tells people enough. You're professional, accessible, and replaceable — the polo makes sure everyone knows all three.
manufacturer: Omex Corporate Services (uniform division, contracted to Haelan Apparel Group)
story_hooks: A stolen Omex polo in the right color grants access to floors that shouldn't be reachable — at least until shift change.
A character wearing one off-duty gets mistaken for on-duty staff and pulled into a situation they can't easily explain their way out of.
Someone selling Omex polos at a Shelf market is either very confused or running a deeper scam.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A crisp, professional polo shirt with corporate precision. Neat, tailored silhouette that reads 'low-level authority' — the uniform of gatekeepers and clipboard holders. Sits at the intersection of casual and formal, designed to be forgettable and trustworthy.
physical_description.fit: Slim to regular through the torso, structured but not restrictive. Sleeves taper slightly at the bicep. Collar stands firm but yields to skin contact. Cut to flatter without drawing attention.
physical_description.primary_material: Synth-blend moisture-wicking jersey — smooth, polymer-based fibers with slight sheen under office fluorescents
physical_description.texture: Butter-smooth surface, almost slick to touch. Fabric has minimal texture; designed for wrinkle resistance and easy care. Seams are cleanly finished, thread-locked at stress points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate blue (reception/client services — cool, neutral, approachable), charcoal (facilities — serious, professional), or white (executive support — sterile, premium). All colorways are muted and corporate-safe.
physical_description.closures: Four-button placket with reinforced buttonholes. Buttons are injection-molded polymer with subtle Omex logo embossing.
distinctive_features: Silver-thread embroidered Omex wordmark on left chest — precise, professional lettering
Employee ID slot sewn into right cuff — functional security theater
Reinforced shoulder seams for durability under repeated wear
Interior neck tape with moisture-wicking treatment
Company laundry code stitched at side seam in tiny letters
Subtle tonal texture knit to mask sweat stains
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 corporate functional wear. Signals employment in the middle management-adjacent service tier. Expensive enough to be quality, cheap enough to be disposable.
physical_description.cultural_context: Uniform of the unglamorous corporate gatekeepers. Wearing this says: 'I work for a mid-tier service provider, I follow dress codes, I have security clearance to exactly one building, I will remember your badge number.' Association with Omex — a sprawling corporate services contractor — marks the wearer as reliable, compliant, and replaceable.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; develops worn collar edges and faint buttonhole stretching after 6-12 months of constant wear. Occasional bleach spots from over-cleaning. Fabric pills slightly at cuffs where ID badges rub. Collars may hold a slight crease if stored poorly.
